Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 27, verse 16:

﴿And Solomon inherited David﴾ [54/b] in his prophethood, his knowledge and his kingship, to the exclusion of the rest of his sons. [[The meaning is not inheritance of wealth, for if it were, Solomon would not have been singled out from among David's other sons. Prophets do not bequeath their wealth, as the Messenger ﷺ informed us in his saying: "We, the company of prophets, do not leave inheritance; what we leave behind is charity." See Ibn Kathir's tafsir (exegesis): 3/359.]] David had nineteen sons. Solomon was given what David was given of kingship, and he was further granted the subjection of the wind and the subjection of the devils. Muqatil said: Solomon was greater than David in kingship and more judicious than him, while David was more devoted in worship than Solomon, and Solomon was more grateful for the blessings of God, exalted is He.

﴿And he said: O mankind, we have been taught the speech of birds﴾. He called the voice of birds "speech" because understanding is obtained from it, just as understanding is obtained from human speech. It is narrated from Ka'b who said: [[These narrations from Ka'b and others, and these details about the speech of birds which the author (may God have mercy on him) mentioned, are derived from the People of the Book, like this narration of Ka'b. The understanding of the verse does not depend on them, and there is no authentic report traced to the Prophet ﷺ in them. Investigating this is of no benefit. And God knows best.]] A wryneck (*warshan*) cried out in the presence of Solomon, peace be upon him, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Build for death, and construct for ruin." A turtle-dove (*fakhitah*) cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Would that these created beings had not been created." A peacock cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: As you judge, so you will be judged." A hoopoe cried out, and he said: "Do you know what this says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy." A *surad* cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Seek forgiveness from God, O sinners." He said: A *tuwtawa* cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Every living thing is dying, and every new thing wears out." A swallow (*khattaf*) cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Send forward some good that you may find it." A dove (*hamamah*) cooed, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, filling His heaven and His earth." A ring-dove (*qumri*) cried out, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." He said: The raven invokes curses upon the tax collector, the kite says: "Everything perishes except God," the partridge says: "Whoever keeps silent is safe," the parrot says: "Woe to the one whose concern is this world," the frog says: "Glory be to my Lord, the Holy," the falcon says: "Glory be to my Lord and praise Him," and the female frog says: "Glory be to the One who is mentioned in every tongue."

And it is narrated from Makhul who said: A *durraj* cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it says?" They said: "No." He said: "It says: The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne."

It is narrated from Farqad al-Sabakhi who said: Solomon passed by a nightingale (*bulbul*) on a tree, moving its head and swaying its tail, and he said to his companions: "Do you know what this nightingale says?" They said: "God and His Prophet know best." He said: "It says: I ate half a date, so let the world perish."

It is also narrated that a group of Jews said to Ibn Abbas: "We will ask you about seven things, and if you inform us, we will believe and affirm." He said: "Ask for understanding, not to trick." They said: "Tell us what the lark (*qunbar*) says in its whistling, the rooster in its crowing, the frog in its croaking, the donkey in its braying, the horse in its neighing, and what the *zarzur* and the *durraj* say?" He said: "Yes. As for the lark, it says: O God, curse the enemies of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. As for the rooster, it says: Remember God, O heedless ones. As for the frog, it says: Glory be to the Worshipped One in the depths of the seas. As for the donkey, it says: O God, curse the tax collector. As for the horse, it says: When the two ranks meet: 'Most Glorified, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.' As for the *zarzur*, it says: O God, I ask You for the provision of each day, day by day, O Provider. As for the *durraj*, it says: The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne." He said: The Jews then embraced Islam, and their Islam was good.

It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, who said: When the vulture (*nasr*) cries out, it says: "O son of Adam, live as you wish, its end is death." When the eagle (*'uqab*) cries out, it says: "In distance from people there is companionship." When the lark cries out, it says: "My God, curse the enemies of the family of Muhammad." When the swallow cries out, it recites: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds," and it prolongs the *dallin* as a reciter prolongs. [Note: the text reads "wa yamudd al-dallin"; rendered as above.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And we have been given of everything﴾: prophets and kings are given. Ibn Abbas said: "Of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter." Muqatil said: "It means prophethood, kingship, the subjection of the jinn, the devils and the winds." ﴿Indeed, this is surely the manifest bounty﴾: the clear excess over what He gave to others besides us.

It is narrated that Solomon, peace be upon him, was given the eastern and western lands of the earth, and he ruled for seven hundred years and six months. He ruled over all the inhabitants of the world: the jinn, mankind, the beasts, the birds and the predators. And in addition to that he was given the speech of every thing, and in his time marvelous crafts were made. [[Narrated by al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak* (2/588), from Ja'far ibn Muhammad. al-Dhahabi said: "This is false."]]

[[In the margin of manuscript "A": His saying "he ruled over all the inhabitants of the world" is open to question, since he (peace be upon him) did not know of Bilqis or her kingdom except through the hoopoe after it informed him of it. Unless we say: he ruled over them after that time. And God knows best.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Solomon were gathered his hosts of jinn and humankind and birds﴾ on his march, ﴿and they were marshalled﴾, meaning they were restrained. Qatadah said: "Over each rank of his troops there were wardens who drove back their first against their last [[In "B": awwaluha ala akhirha (their first against their last).]] so that they would not advance ahead in the march. The *wazi'* (warden) is the one who holds back, and he is the *naqib* (overseer)." Muqatil said: "*Yuza'un* means they are driven on." Al-Suddi said: "They are halted." It was also said: "They are gathered." The root of *wazʿ* is restraint and prevention.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Solomon's encampment was a hundred *farsakh* (a unit of distance), twenty-five of them for humankind, twenty-five for the jinn, twenty-five for the wild beasts, and twenty-five for the birds. He had a thousand tents of glass set on wooden poles, in which were three hundred *sarihah* [[Meaning: a married wife.]] and seven hundred *sariyyah* (concubines). He would command the violent wind and it would lift him, and he would command the gentle breeze and it would carry him along. God revealed to him while he was travelling between the heaven and the earth: 'Indeed I have increased your kingdom, so that no creature speaks a word except that the wind brings it to you; it will inform you...'" [[Al-Hakim recorded it in *al-Mustadrak* from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "It reached us that Solomon..." (2/589), and it is weak.]]

He said, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants﴾. It is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ka'b, who said: When Solomon rode, he carried his family, his servants and his retinue. He had prepared kitchens and bakeries, which he carried with him, containing great iron cauldrons and large pots, each pot able to hold ten camels. He had also prepared open grounds for the animals in front of him, where the cooks cooked and the bakers baked, while the animals ran before him between heaven and earth, and the wind carried them. He travelled from Istakhr to Yemen and passed by the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Solomon said: "This is the abode of the emigration of a Prophet at the end of time. Blessed is whoever believes in him, and blessed is whoever follows him." He saw around the House idols worshipped besides Allah. When Solomon passed the House, it wept [55/a]. Allah revealed to the House: "What makes you weep?" It said: "O Lord, it makes me weep that this is a Prophet among Your prophets, and a people among Your friends, who passed by me and did not descend or pray at me, while idols are worshipped around me besides You." Allah revealed to it: "Do not weep, for I will fill you with prostrating faces, and I will send down in you a new Qur'an, and I will raise up from you a Prophet at the end of time, the most beloved of My prophets to Me. I will make in you inhabitants from My creation who worship Me, and I will prescribe for My servants an obligation by which they will hasten to you like the swooping of vultures to their nest, and they will yearn for you as a she-camel yearns for her young and as a dove yearns for her egg. I will purify you from the idols and the worshippers of devils." [[This report and similar ones are among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources) which Wahb and Ka'b used to relate, and there is no authentic text in them on which proof can be based.]] Then Solomon proceeded until he passed through the valley of al-Sadir, a valley of al-Ta'if, and came upon the valley of the ants. Thus said Ka'b: it is a valley in al-Ta'if. Qatadah and Muqatil said: it is a land in al-Sham. It was also said: it is a valley which the jinn inhabited, and those ants were their mounts. [[Ibn Kathir said (3/360): "As for those among the exegetes who say that this valley was in the land of al-Sham or elsewhere, or that this ant had two wings like a fly, or other such sayings, there is no benefit in them."]] Nawf al-Himyari said: the ants of that valley were like flies. [[Ibn Kathir said in the same place: "I saw it vocalised with a ya' below, but it is with a ba' above, and that is a misreading, and Allah knows best. The point is that Solomon, peace be upon him, understood her words and smiled laughing at that, and this is a very great matter."]] It was also said: they were like large camels. The well-known view is that they were small ants. Al-Sha'bi said: that ant had two wings. It was also said: it was a lame ant, and she called out: ﴿A certain ant said: O ants, enter your dwellings﴾, and she did not say "ادخلن" (enter, feminine plural), because when He gave them speech like that of the children of Adam, they were addressed with the address of the children of Adam. ﴿Lest Solomon and his hosts crush you﴾, meaning lest they break you, and "الحطم" (al-hatm) means breaking, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾. So Solomon heard her words, and no creature spoke except that the wind carried that and cast it into Solomon's ears. Muqatil said: Solomon heard her speech from three miles away. Al-Dahhak said: the name of that ant was Tahiyah. Muqatil said: her name was Jarma. [[There is no benefit in investigating the attributes of this ant and its name, and there is no report from the Messenger (ﷺ) to which one may turn. It is sufficient for us what Allah the Exalted has told us of the speech of the ant, Solomon's understanding of it, and what is indicated in that. And Allah knows best. See also: al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah of Ibn Kathir: 2/19.]] If it is said: How can crushing by Solomon and his hosts be conceived, when the wind was carrying Solomon and his hosts on a carpet between heaven and earth? It is said: his soldiers were riders, and among them were those on foot on the ground, for the ground was folded up for them. It was also said: this may have been before Allah subjected the wind to Solomon. The people of tafsir said: the ants knew that Solomon was a Prophet in whom there was no tyranny or injustice. The meaning of the verse is: "If you do not enter your dwellings, they will trample you and will not perceive you." It is reported that when Solomon reached the valley of the ants, he held back his hosts until the ants had entered their dwellings.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 19:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her speech﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: Most of the laughter of the prophets was smiling (tabassum). And His saying ﴿laughing﴾ means: smiling. It was said: at first it was smiling, and at last it was laughter.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to me, Amr, that is Ibn al-Harith, informed us, al-Nadr informed us, that he narrated to him from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Aisha, who said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughing fully so that I could see his uvula; he only used to smile [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter: "So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys": 8/578, and by Muslim in Istisqa' prayer, chapter on seeking refuge when seeing the wind, no. (899): 2/616-617, and the author mentioned it in Masabih al-Sunnah: 1/1073.]]. Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Khuza'i informed us, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us, Abu Isa narrated to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz', who said: I never saw anyone who smiled more than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Manaqib, chapter on the cheerfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ): 10/124, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith. It has been narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz', something similar to this." Also narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/190, and the author mentioned it in Masabih al-Sunnah, no. (3686).]].

Muqatil said: The laughter of Sulayman was at the speech of the ant, out of wonder, because when a person sees something he is not accustomed to, he wonders and laughs. Then Sulayman praised his Lord for what He had bestowed upon him.

﴿And he said: My Lord, inspire me﴾ i.e., grant me inspiration, ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that You approve, and admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾. That is: admit me among their number, record my name with their names, and gather me in their company. Ibn Abbas said: He means with Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, and those after them of the prophets. It was said: admit me into Paradise by Your mercy among Your righteous servants.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾, meaning he sought them and searched for them. Tafaqqud (inspection for what is missing) is seeking what has been lost. The meaning of the verse is that he sought what was missing from the birds, ﴿and said, "Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe?"﴾, meaning: what is the matter with the hoopoe that I do not see it? The Arabs say, "Why do I see you downcast?", meaning, "What is the matter with you?" The hoopoe is a well-known bird.

The reason for his inspecting for the hoopoe and asking about it was said to be his neglect of his turn (nawba, the rotation of duty). Sulayman, when he alighted at a place, would have the birds shade him and his army from the sun. The sun struck him from the spot where the hoopoe was, so he looked and saw that it was absent.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the hoopoe was Sulayman's guide to water. It knew the location of water and could see the water beneath the earth as one sees it in a glass, and it knew how near or far it was, so it would peck at the ground. Then the devils would come, split the ground open, and extract the water. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When Ibn Abbas mentioned this, Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to him, "O Wassaf, look at what you are saying! A boy among us places a trap and throws dust over it, and the hoopoe comes and does not see the trap until it falls into its neck." Ibn Abbas said to him, "Woe to you! When decree comes, it blocks sight." In another narration: "When the decree and the destiny descend, reason departs and sight is blinded."[[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2/405-406, who authenticated it according to the conditions of al-Shaykhayn (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and al-Tabari: 19/144. al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/348.]]

Sulayman alighted at a place and needed water. They searched but found none, so he inspected for the hoopoe so that it could guide him to water. He said, ﴿What is the matter with me that I do not see the hoopoe?﴾, on the assumption that it was among his troops and he simply could not see it. Then doubt about its absence came over him, so he said, ﴿Or is he among the absent?﴾, meaning: "Was he among the absent?" The mim here is a supplementary (silah) letter. It was also said that "am" here means "bal" (rather). Then he threatened it for its absence, saying, ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 21:**

﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment.﴾ The scholars differed about the punishment he threatened. The most apparent of these views is that he would pluck out his feathers and his tail, and throw him into the sun, mangy, unable to defend himself against ants or the creatures of the earth.[[Al-Tabari adopted this view and mentioned no other: 19/146. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/349-350, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/361.]] Muqatil and Ibn Hayyan said: "I will smear him with tar and expose him to the sun." It was also said: "I will confine him in a cage." It was said: "I will separate him from his mate." It was said: "I will imprison him with his opposite."

﴿Or I will slaughter him﴾, meaning I will cut his throat. ﴿Or he must bring me a clear authority﴾, meaning a clear proof, in his absence, and an evident excuse. Ibn Kathir recited "la-ya'tiyannani" with two nuns, the first of them doubled, while the others recited it with a single doubled nun.

The reason for the hoopoe's absence, as the scholars related it,[[What the author attributes to the scholars is evidently among the reports that lack a chain of transmission, and such detailed accounts are strange.]] was that when Solomon finished building Bayt al-Maqdis, he resolved to set out for the land of the Haram. He prepared for the journey and took with him from the jinn, mankind, the devils, the birds and the beasts so many that his encampment extended a hundred farsakhs. The wind carried them. When he arrived at the Haram, he stayed there as long as God willed. Each day during his stay in Makkah he would sacrifice five thousand camels, slaughter five thousand bulls and twenty thousand sheep.[[In "B": kabsh (ram).]] He said to the nobles of his people who were present: "This is a place from which will come a Prophet of the Arabs with such and such a description. He will be given victory over all who oppose him, and his awe will reach a distance of a month's journey. Near and far are equal before him in truth, and the blame of no blamer will deter him in God's cause." They said: "By which religion will he follow, O Prophet of God?" He said: "He will follow the religion of the Hanifiyyah (the primordial monotheistic faith), so blessed is whoever meets him and believes in him." They said: "How long is it between us and his coming, O Prophet of God?" He said: "About a thousand years. Let whoever is present among you convey it to the one who is absent, for he is the master of the prophets and the seal of the messengers."

He remained in Makkah until he completed his rites, then left Makkah in the morning and headed toward Yemen. He reached Sana'a at midday, a journey of a month. He saw a beautiful land whose greenery was radiant, and he wished to alight there to pray and take his midday meal. When he alighted, he said to the hoopoe: "Solomon has occupied himself with dismounting. Rise toward the sky and look at the length and breadth of the world." The hoopoe did so, looked to the right and left, and saw a garden belonging to Bilqis. He inclined toward the greenery, descended into it, and found a hoopoe, and alighted beside it. The name of Solomon's hoopoe was "Ya'fur," and the name of the hoopoe of Yemen was "Infir." The Yemeni hoopoe said to Solomon's hoopoe: "From where have you come, and where are you heading?" He replied: "I have come from al-Sham with my companion Solomon son of Dawud." He asked: "And who is Solomon?" He said: "The king of the jinn, mankind, the devils, the birds, the beasts and the winds. And where are you from?" He said: "I am from this land." He asked: "And who is its king?" He said: "A woman called Bilqis. Your companion has a great kingdom, but Bilqis's kingdom is not beneath his, for she is queen of all Yemen, and under her hand are twelve thousand commanders, and under the hand of each commander are a hundred thousand fighters. Will you go with me to see her kingdom?" He said: "I fear that Solomon will miss me at the time of prayer, when he needs water." The Yemeni hoopoe said: "Your companion would be pleased if you brought him news of this queen." So he went with it and looked at Bilqis and her kingdom, and did not return to Solomon until the time of 'Asr.

He said: When Solomon dismounted and the time of prayer came upon him, and he had alighted where there was no water, he asked mankind, the jinn and the devils about water, but they did not know. He then inspected the birds and found the hoopoe missing. He summoned the chief of the birds, who was the eagle-hawk (al-nasr), and asked him about the hoopoe. He said: "May God set the King right, I do not know where it is, and I did not send it anywhere." At that, Solomon became angry and said: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾, the verse in full. Then he summoned the eagle, lord of the birds, and said: "Bring me the hoopoe at once." The eagle raised itself above the sky until it clung to the air, and looked at the world like a dish before one of you. Then it turned right and left, and there was the hoopoe coming from the direction of Yemen. The eagle swooped toward it, intending to seize it. When the hoopoe saw this, it knew the eagle meant it harm, so it appealed to it, saying: "By the right of God who gave you strength and power over me, spare me and do not harm me." He said: The eagle turned away from it and said to it: "Woe to you! May your mother be bereft of you! The Prophet of God has sworn that he will punish you or slaughter you." Then they both flew off toward Solomon. When they reached the encampment, the hawk and the birds met it and said: "Woe to you! Where have you been absent on this day of yours? The Prophet of God has threatened you, and they informed him of what he had said." The hoopoe said: "Did the Messenger of God not make an exception?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Or he must bring me a clear authority." He said: "Then I have been saved." Then the eagle and the hoopoe flew until they came to Solomon, who was sitting on his throne. The eagle said: "I have brought it to you, O Prophet of God." When the hoopoe drew near, it lifted its head, let down its tail and wings, dragging them on the ground out of humility before Solomon. When it came close to him, he seized its head, pulled it toward himself, and said: "Where were you? I will surely punish you with a severe punishment." The hoopoe said: "O Prophet of God, remember your standing before God the Exalted." When Solomon heard that, he trembled and pardoned it. Then he asked it: "What has delayed you from me?" The hoopoe replied with what God related about it in His words: ﴿So he remained not long.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 22–23:**

﴿He stayed not long﴾. ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read ﴿famakatha﴾ with a fatḥah on the kāf (*famakatha*). The others read it with a ḍammah (*famakutha*). Both are dialectal variants (*lughatān*). ﴿Not long﴾ means not for a long time. ﴿He said: I have encompassed [knowledge of] what you have not encompassed﴾. Iḥāṭah (encompassing) is knowledge of a thing from all its aspects. He is saying: I know what you do not know, and I have reached what neither you nor your armies have reached. ﴿And I have come to you from Saba'﴾. Abū ʿAmr and al-Bazzī, on the authority of Ibn Kathīr, read *Saba'* (with a fatḥah on the bāʾ and a hamzah at the end, *Saba'a*) [and *li-Saba'*, in Surat Saba', with a fatḥah on the hamzah]. [Qawwās, on the authority of Ibn Kathīr, read it unvocalized with a sukūn and without a hamzah.]¹ The others read it with inflection (*al-ijrāʾ*, i.e., with tanwīn, as a declined noun). Whoever does not decline it (*lam yajurrahu*) takes it as the name of a place. Whoever declines it takes it as the name of a man. It has come in a ḥadīth that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about Saba', and he said: "He was a man who had ten sons; six of them went to the right (*tayammana*), and four went to the left (*tashāʾama*)."² ﴿With certain news﴾, that is, with true information.

﴿Then Sulaymān said: And what is that?﴾ He said: ﴿I found a woman ruling over them﴾, ﴿I found a woman ruling over them﴾. Her name was Bilqīs, daughter of Sharāḥīl, from the descendants of Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān. Her father was a king of great standing. Forty kings were born to him, and she was the last of them. He ruled the whole land of Yemen, and he would say to the kings of the outlying regions: "None of you is my equal." He refused to marry among them, so they married him to a woman of the jinn called Rayḥānah bint al-Sakan, and she bore him Bilqīs. [He had no other child besides her. It has come in a ḥadīth that one of Bilqīs's parents was a jinnī.³] When Bilqīs's father died, she coveted the kingship and asked her people to pledge allegiance to her. Some of them obeyed her, and others disobeyed her. They made a man king over themselves, and they split into two factions, each of which took control of a part of the land of Yemen. Then the man whom they had made king behaved badly toward the people of his realm, to the point that he would reach out his hand to the women of his subjects and commit fornication with them. His people wanted to depose him, but they could not overcome him. When Bilqīs saw that...

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 27, verses 24–27:

Jealousy seized her, so she sent to him [saying]: "Are you offering yourself to him?" The king answered her and said: "What prevented me from beginning the proposal to you was only my despair of you." She said: "I am not averse to you. [He is] a suitable and noble match. So gather the men of my people and propose to me before them." He gathered them and proposed to her before them. They said: "We do not see her doing this." He said to them: "She has initiated [the proposal] to me, so I would like you to hear her words." They came to her and mentioned it to her. She said: "Yes, I have come to love the young man." So they married her to him. When she was escorted to him, she went out with many people from her retinue (ḥashm). When she came to him, she gave him wine until he became drunk. Then she cut off his head and returned to her house in the night. When the people awoke, they saw the king slain, and his head hung on the gate of her house. So they knew that this marriage had been a deception and a trick from her. They gathered around her and said: "You are more worthy of this kingdom than anyone else." So they made her queen (famallakūhā).[[Ibn Kathir referred to this story and attributed it to al-Tha'labi and others. See: al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 2 / 21.]]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yusuf (al-Hafiz) informed us, Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Uthman ibn al-Haytham informed us, Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that the people of Persia had made the daughter of Chosroes their ruler, he said: "A people will never prosper who entrust their affairs to a woman."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter "The Book of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Chosroes and Caesar": 8 / 126, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10 / 76. He said: "They are agreed that a woman is not suitable to be an imam or a judge, because the imam needs to go out to establish the matter of jihad and to undertake the affairs of the Muslims, and the judge needs to come forward to decide disputes, and a woman is 'awrah (a part that must be concealed) and not suitable to come forward; and she is too weak to carry out most affairs; and because a woman is deficient, while leadership and judgeship are among the complete forms of authority, so only a complete man is suitable for them..."]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And she has been given of everything﴾ — [meaning] what kings need of equipment and provisions. ﴿And she has a mighty throne﴾ — a huge throne, which was made of gold, adorned with pearls, red rubies and green emeralds, its legs were of ruby and emerald, and upon it were seven canopies, and on each canopy was a closed door. Ibn Abbas said: The throne of Bilqis was thirty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the sky (al-sama') was thirty cubits. Muqatil said: Its length was eighty cubits, and its height in the sky (al-hawa')[[In (B): "al-hawa'" (air).]] was eighty cubits. It was also said: Its length was eighty cubits, its width forty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.

﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and has barred them from the way, so they are not guided, so that they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal and what you disclose. Allah — there is no god but Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾ He said: ﴿We shall see whether you have told the truth or were of the liars.﴾

﴿Alla yasjudū﴾: Abu Ja'far and al-Kisa'i read "Alla yasjudū" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation of the lām. When they stop, they stop at "alā yā" (alā yā), then begin with "isjudū" (prostrate), meaning: "Alā yā hā'ulā'i isjudū" (Oh, these people, prostrate!). They took it as a command from Allah, a new (mustaʼnaf) sentence, and they omitted "hā'ulā'" (these), being satisfied with the indication of "yā" (O) upon it. Some of them cited from the Arabs a hearing (samā'): "Alā yā irḥamūnā" (Oh, have mercy upon us), meaning "Alā yā qawmu" (Oh, my people). Al-Akhtal said:

"Alā yā islamī yā Hind, Hind of Banī Bakr...
Even if our neighbours have passed away until the end of time."[[The verse is in Lisan al-Arab, under the root (ʿ-d-w). It is also cited by al-Tabari: 19 / 149.]]

He means: "Alā yā islamī yā Hind" (Oh, Hind, be at peace). On this reading, "alā" is a parenthetical statement, not part of the story, either from the hoopoe or from Solomon. Abu Ubayda said: This is a new command from Allah, meaning: O people, prostrate! Others read "allā yasjudū" with shadda (doubled lām), meaning: "Satan made their deeds appealing to them so that they would not prostrate." ﴿To Allah who brings forth the khab'*﴾, i.e. the hidden, concealed thing. ﴿In the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e. what is concealed. Most of the exegetes said: The khab' of the sky is rain, and the khab' of the earth is plants. In the recitation of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): "yukhriju al-khab'a min al-samawāti wal-arḍ," and "min" and "fī" are interchangeable. The Arabs say: "La-astakhrijanna al-'ilma fīkum," meaning: "from you." It was also said: The meaning of al-khab' is the unseen, meaning: He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth.

﴿And knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾: al-Kisa'i, Hafs, from Asim, read both with the letter "tā'" (you), because the beginning of the verse is an address according to al-Kisa'i's reading with the light pronunciation of "alā". The others read with "yā'" (he).

﴿Allah — there is no god but Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: meaning, He is the one deserving of worship and prostration, not anyone else. And the throne of the queen of Sheba, though it is great, is small and insignificant in comparison to His throne, Mighty and Majestic. Here ends the speech of the hoopoe.

When the hoopoe had finished his speech,

﴿[Solomon] said﴾ to the hoopoe: ﴿We shall see whether you have told the truth regarding what you reported, or were of the liars?﴾ The hoopoe then guided them to the water, so they dug the wells (rakāyā) [Note: rakāyā is the plural of rakiyya, meaning a well], and the people and the animals were watered. Then Solomon wrote a letter: "From the servant of Allah, Sulayman ibn Dawud, to Bilqis, queen of Sheba: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Peace upon those who follow guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission." Ibn Jurayj said: Sulayman did not add to what Allah related in His Book. Qatada said: Thus the prophets used to write brief sentences, neither lengthy nor verbose. When he had written the letter, he sealed it with musk and stamped it with his ring. Then he said to the hoopoe: ﴿Take this letter of mine, and deliver it to them.﴾

Qatadah and Muqatil said: the people of her consultation were three hundred and thirteen men, each of whom was over ten thousand. He said: they came and took their seats.

﴿She said﴾, namely Bilqis: ﴿O chiefs﴾, and they were the nobles and elders of the people: ﴿Indeed, there has been delivered to me a noble letter.﴾

'Ata' and al-Dahhak said: she called it "noble" because it was sealed. Ibn Jurayj narrated from 'Ata', from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The honour of a letter is its seal." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat through the narration of Muhammad ibn Marwan, who is al-Saddi al-Saghir, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn Abbas. It was also recorded by al-Qada'i in the Musnad of al-Bayhaqi. Muhammad ibn Marwan is abandoned (matruk). See: al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (125); Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/99.]] Qatadah and Muqatil said: "a noble letter" means a good one, and this is the view preferred by al-Zajjaj, who said: what it contains is good. It is reported from Ibn Abbas that "noble" means honourable because of the honour of its sender. It was also said: she called it noble because it began with "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." [[Al-Tabari recorded these sayings in his Tafsir: 19/153.]] Then she clarified who the letter was from, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is from Sulayman﴾.

﴿Indeed it is from Sulayman﴾ and it begins with: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾. ﴿Do not exalt yourselves against me﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, do not be arrogant toward me. It was also said: do not magnify yourselves or rise above me. Its meaning is: do not refuse to answer, for refusing to answer is a form of haughtiness and arrogance. ﴿And come to me in submission﴾, meaning as believers, obedient. It was said: this is from al-Islam (submission, becoming Muslim), and it was said: it is from al-istislam (surrendering).

﴿She said: O chiefs, advise me in my affair﴾, that is, give me your counsel regarding what has come before me, and answer me concerning that on which I consult you. ﴿I would not decide an affair﴾, meaning I would not judge or conclude it, ﴿until you are present with me﴾ [that is: until you attend]. [The words between the brackets are omitted from manuscript "A".]

﴿They said﴾, responding to her: ﴿We are possessed of strength﴾ in fighting, ﴿and possessed of great might﴾ in war. Muqatil said: by strength they meant a large number, and by great might, courage. This was an indirect hint from them at fighting, should she order them to do so. Then they said: ﴿But the command is yours﴾, O queen, regarding fighting and abandoning it, ﴿so consider﴾ the matter with your judgment, ﴿what you will command﴾, and you will find us obedient to your command.

﴿She said﴾, Bilqis, answering them regarding their indirect suggestion of fighting: ﴿Indeed, when kings enter a town﴾ by force, ﴿they ruin it﴾, they devastate it, ﴿and they make the honored of its people humbled﴾, that is, they humiliate its nobles and elders so that their rule may be established. She warned them about Sulayman's march toward them and his entry into their land. The report of her words ends here, and Allah confirmed her statement, saying: ﴿And thus they do﴾, that is, just as she said, so they do.

Then she said: ﴿Indeed, I am sending them a gift﴾. A gift (hadiyyah) is a present given as a gesture of goodwill. Balqis was an intelligent woman who had been trained in governance and had governed well. She said to the chiefs of her people: "I am sending them, that is, to Sulayman and his people, a gift, by which I will placate him concerning my kingdom and test him to see whether he is a king or a prophet. If he is a king, he will accept the gift and go away. But if he is a prophet, he will not accept the gift, and he will be satisfied with nothing from us except that we follow his religion." This is the statement of the Exalted: ﴿So I will wait and see with what the messengers return﴾. [So she sent to him] [[The phrase in brackets is omitted in manuscript "A".]] servant boys and servant girls. Ibn 'Abbas said: "She dressed them in one style of clothing so that the male could not be distinguished from the female." Mujahid said: "The boys were dressed in the clothing of girls, and the girls were dressed in the clothing of boys." They differed about their number. Ibn 'Abbas said: "One hundred servant boys and one hundred servant girls." [[Al-wasifah: the slave girl.]] Mujahid [and Muqatil] [[The phrase in brackets is omitted in manuscript "A".]] said: "Two hundred boys and two hundred girls."

Qatadah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "She sent to him a brick of gold wrapped in silk and brocade." Thabit al-Bunani said: "She sent him plates of gold in cases of brocade." It was also said: "They were four bricks of gold." Wahb and others said: "Balqis chose five hundred boys and five hundred girls. She dressed the boys in the clothing of girls and placed bracelets of gold on their forearms, collars of gold around their necks, and earrings and ear-pendants set with various kinds of jewels. She dressed the girls in the clothing of boys: the long robes and the belts. She mounted the girls on five hundred she-mules [[Female mules.]] and the boys on five hundred horses, and on every horse was a bridle of gold set with jewels, and its covering was of colored brocade. She sent him five hundred bricks of gold and five hundred bricks of silver, and a crown encrusted with pearls and rubies of great height. She also sent him musk, ambergris, and aloes wood. She took a box and placed inside it a precious pearl that was not drilled, and a bead of carnelian that was drilled with a crooked hole. She called a man of the nobles of her people named al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, and she joined with him men of her people who were men of opinion and intellect. She wrote a letter with him, containing a copy of the gift, and she said in it: 'If you are a prophet, distinguish between the servant girls and the servant boys, tell me what is in the box before you open it, drill the pearl with a straight hole, and thread a string into the drilled bead without the treatment of any human or jinn.' Balqis then instructed the boys, saying: 'When Sulayman speaks to you, speak to him in a feminine and softened manner resembling the speech of women.' And she instructed the girls to speak to him in a harsh manner resembling the speech of men.

Then she said to the messenger: 'Look at the man when you enter upon him. If he looks at you with a glance of anger, know that he is a king, and do not let his appearance frighten you, for we are greater than him. But if you see the man cheerful and gentle, know that he is a sent prophet. Then understand his words and return the answer.' The messenger set off with the gifts, and the hoopoe came hurrying to Sulayman and informed him of the entire news. Sulayman then commanded the jinn to strike bricks of gold and bricks of silver, and they did so. Then he commanded them to spread out from the place where he was to a distance of nine farsakhs a single open plain paved with bricks of gold and silver, and to place around the plain a wall whose battlements were of gold and silver. Then he said: 'What animals are more beautiful than what you have seen on land and sea?' They said: 'O Prophet of Allah, we saw animals in the sea of such-and-such, striped, of varied colors, with wings, manes, and forelocks.' He said: 'Bring them to me now.' They brought them, and he said: 'Tie them on the right side of the plain and on its left, upon the bricks of gold and silver, and throw their fodder before them.' Then he said to the jinn: 'Bring me your children,' and a great multitude gathered. He stationed them on the right side of the plain and on its left. Then Sulayman sat in his assembly upon his throne, and four thousand chairs were set for him on his right, and the same number on his left. He commanded the devils to line up in ranks extending farsakhs, and he commanded mankind, and they lined up farsakhs, and he commanded the wild beasts, the predators, the creeping creatures, and the birds, and they lined up farsakhs on his right and his left. When the people drew near the plain, [57/a] and they looked upon the kingdom of Sulayman and saw animals the likes of which their eyes had never seen, dunging upon the bricks of gold and silver, their selves were humbled, and they threw away the gifts they had with them. In some narrations, when Sulayman commanded that the plain be paved with bricks of gold and silver, he commanded them to leave on their path a space equal to the size of the bricks they had with them. When the envoys saw the place of the bricks empty while the whole ground was paved, they feared they would be accused of this, so they threw what they had with them in that place. When they saw the devils, they beheld a strange sight and were terrified. The devils said to them: 'Pass on, there is no harm upon you.' So they passed by battalion after battalion of jinn, mankind, birds, creeping creatures, predators, and wild beasts, until they stood before Sulayman. Sulayman looked at them with a kindly glance and a cheerful face, and said: 'What is behind you?' The leader of the people informed him of what they had come for, and gave him the letter of the queen. He looked into it, then said: 'Where is the box?' They brought it, and he shook it. Gabriel came and informed him of what was in the box. He said: 'Indeed, in it is a precious pearl that is not drilled, and a carnelian bead that is drilled with a crooked hole.' The messenger said: 'You have spoken truly. So drill the pearl and thread the string into the bead.' Sulayman said: 'Who will drill it for me?' He asked mankind, then the jinn, but they did not have the knowledge of that. Then he asked the devils, and they said: 'We will send for the worm.' The worm came and took a hair in its mouth and entered the pearl until it came out the other side. Sulayman said to it: 'What is your need?' It said: 'Make my provision in the tree.' He said: 'That is yours.'

It is also narrated that a worm which lives in the willow came and said: 'I will thread the string through the hole on condition that my provision be in the willow.' So he granted her that, and she took the string in her mouth, entered the hole, and came out the other side. Then he said: 'Who will thread this bead onto the string?' A white worm said: 'I am for it, O Messenger of Allah.' The worm took the string in its mouth, entered the hole, and came out the other side. Sulayman said: 'What is your need?' She said: 'Make my provision in the fruits.' He said: 'That is yours.' Then he distinguished between the servant girls and the servant boys by commanding them to wash their faces and hands. The girl would take water from the vessel with one of her hands, then pour it onto the other hand, then strike her face with it. The boy, as he took it from the vessel, would strike his face with it. The girl would pour the water over the inner part of her forearm, and the boy over the back of the forearm. The girl would pour the water in a flow, and the boy would let the water run down over his hands in a stream. Thus he distinguished them by that. Then Sulayman returned the gift, as God the Exalted said: ﴿So when [the envoy] came to Sulayman, he said: "Would you provide me with wealth?"﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 36:

﴿Then when he (the messenger) came to Solomon, he said: "Will you provide me with wealth?"﴾ Hamzah and Ya'qub recited: "Atumiddunnii" (ﺃَﺗُﻤِﺪُّﻭﻧِّﻲ) with one doubled nun and with the ya' retained (the ya' being the pronoun "me"), while the others recited it with two light nuns. Ahl al-Hijaz (the people of Hijaz) and Basra retain the ya', while the others omit it.

﴿What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you.﴾ That is: what Allah has given me of prophethood, religion, wisdom and kingship is better, ﴿more excellent﴾, than what He has given you.

﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift.﴾ Because you are people of boasting and vying with one another in worldly matters, you rejoice in the giving of gifts among yourselves. As for me, I do not rejoice in them, and the world is not among my needs, because Allah the Exalted has established me in it and given me of it what He has given no one else, and yet, along with that, He has honored me with religion and prophethood.

Then he said to al-Mundhir ibn Amr, the leader of the delegation: ﴿Return to them.﴾

ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ — "Return to them" — with the gift (bi-l-hadiyyah). ﴿فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بِجُنُودٍ لَا قِبَلَ لَهُمْ﴾ "then We shall certainly come to them with hosts that they have no power to withstand" (la qibala lahum: lā ṭāqata lahum) "by them, and We shall certainly drive them out of it" — that is, out of their land and their country, which is Saba' — "humiliated, and they will be abased," meaning they will be humbled if they do not come to me in submission.

Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: When Bilqis's envoys returned to her from Solomon, she said: "I have recognised, by God, that this is no mere king, and we have no power against him." So she sent to Solomon: "I am coming to you with the nobles of my people, so that I may see what your command is and what you call to from your religion." Then she ordered her throne to be placed in the innermost of seven chambers, one within another, in the innermost of seven palaces that belonged to her. Then the doors were locked behind it, and she appointed guards to protect it. Then she said to those she left in charge of her authority: "Guard what is with you and my throne of kingship; let no one reach it, and let no one see it until I come to you." Then she ordered a herald to call out among the people of her kingdom, informing them of the departure, and she set out toward Solomon with twelve thousand qayl (chieftains) from the kings of Yemen, under each qayl were many thousands.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Solomon was a man of awe-inspiring dignity; no matter would be begun with him until he himself asked about it. One day he went out and sat on his royal throne, and he saw a dust cloud close to him. He said: "What is this?" They said: "Bilqis, and she has descended at this place near us." It had been at a distance of one farsakh (league) from Solomon. Ibn 'Abbas said: The distance between Kufa and al-Hira was about one farsakh. Then Solomon turned at that moment to his troops.

﴿قَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ "He said: 'O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?'" That is: believers (mu'minin). Ibn 'Abbas said: obedient (ta'i'in). They differed about the reason for which Solomon ordered the bringing of her throne. Most of them said: because Solomon knew that if she embraced Islam, her wealth would become unlawful to him, so he wished to take her throne before its taking became unlawful to him through her Islam [[Narrated by al-Tabari (19/160) from Qatadah.]]. His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Disguise her throne for her"﴾. He means: change her throne into a form that she will not recognize when she sees it. Sulayman acted this way, as Wahb, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others mentioned, because the devils feared that Sulayman would marry her and that she would disclose the secrets of the jinn to him, since her mother was a jinniyyah. If she bore him a son, they would no longer be free of subjugation to Sulayman and his descendants after him. So they spoke ill of her to make him averse to her, and they said: "There is something wrong with her intellect, her leg is like a donkey's hoof, and she has hair on her shins." **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 27, verses 42–43:**

﴿So when she came, it was said: "Is your throne like this?" She said: "It is as if it were it."﴾ Muqatil said: She recognized it, but she made it seem doubtful to them, just as they had made it seem doubtful to her. Ikrimah said: She was wise. She did not say "Yes," fearing that she would be lying, and she did not say "No," fearing denial. She said: "As if it were it," so Sulayman recognized her full intelligence, since she neither confirmed nor denied. It was also said that the matter of the throne was confused for her, because she had left it in a room behind seven locked doors, with the keys in her possession. It was said to her: "Indeed, this is your throne," and the locking of the doors did not avail her. So she said: ﴿And we were given knowledge﴾ of the soundness of Sulayman's prophethood through the earlier signs concerning the gift and the messengers, ﴿before it﴾, that is, before the sign concerning the throne, ﴿and we were Muslims﴾, meaning submissive and obedient to the command of Sulayman. It was also said that her statement "And we were given knowledge before it" was spoken by Sulayman, meaning: "We were given knowledge of Allah and of His power to do what He wills, before this woman, and we were Muslims." This is the saying of Mujahid. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 19/167. It is the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Kathir: 3/366 approved it, supporting it by noting that she only openly professed Islam after entering the palace.]] It was also said: the meaning is "And we were given knowledge of her Islam and her coming in obedience before her coming, and we were Muslims, obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah prevented her﴾. That is, what she used to worship besides Allah, which is the sun, prevented her from worshipping Allah. In other words, the worship of the sun barred her from monotheism (tawhid) and the worship of Allah. According to this interpretation, "mā" (ما) is in the nominative position (rafʿ, the grammatical case of the subject) [[See al-Tabari 19/167; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/362.]].

It was also said: the meaning is [she was barred from worshipping Allah, not because of any deficiency in her intellect, as the jinn said: "Indeed, there is something in her intellect," but rather she used to worship besides Allah]. [[In manuscript "B" the phrase reads: "This prevented her from worshipping Allah, what she used to worship besides Allah."]] It was also said: the meaning is "And Sulayman barred her from what she used to worship besides Allah," meaning he prevented her from that and stood between her and it. In this case, the position of "mā" is accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case of the object).

﴿Indeed, she was from a people who were disbelievers﴾. This is a resumptive statement (istiʾnaf, a new independent sentence). Allah, Exalted, informs that she was from a people who worshipped the sun. She grew up among them and knew nothing but the worship of the sun.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 27, verse 44:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿It was said to her, "Enter the palace."﴾ [The verse]. The reason was that Sulayman wanted to look at her feet and shins without asking her to uncover them, after the devils had said that her feet were like a donkey's hoof and that she had hair on her shins. He ordered the devils, and they built for him a *sarh* (palace), that is, a castle of glass. It was also said that it was a house of glass, as white as water. It was also said: the *sarh* is the courtyard of the house. He caused water to flow beneath it and placed in it every kind of sea creature, fish, frogs and others. Then he placed his throne in its middle and sat upon it, and the birds, the jinn and the humans gathered around him. It was also said that he made a courtyard of glass and placed beneath it images of fish and frogs, so that whoever saw it thought it was water. It was also said that he built the *sarh* only to test her understanding, just as she had tested them with the servants and the maidservants [[See what we have quoted from Ibn Kathir commenting on these narrations above. Al-Tabari said (19/169): "It is permissible in my view that Sulayman ordered the building of the *sarh* for both reasons: the one stated by Wahb, and the one stated by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, to test her intelligence and to look at her shin and her foot, so as to know the truth of what was said about her."

The truth is that Sulayman, peace be upon him, built the *sarh* in order to show her the greatness of his kingdom and his authority, and that Allah, glorified and exalted, had given him kingship and the means of prosperity and civilization that He had not given her, not to mention prophethood, which is above kingship, and above which there is no blessing. Far be it from Sulayman, peace be upon him, who asked Allah to give him a judgment that would match His judgment, that Allah granted him, to resort to such a stratagem in order to look at what Allah had forbidden him, namely her shins. He is far above that and more exalted.

Had she not seen in Sulayman the firm religion and the lofty character that he had, she would not have submitted to him when he invited her to Allah, the One, the Truth, nor would she have repented of her worship of the stars and the sun, and submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds. See: *al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at* by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahba, pp. 249–250.]] When he sat on the throne, he summoned Bilqis, and when she came, it was said to her, "Enter the palace."

﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a deep water﴾ [27:44], that is, the greatest body of water, ﴿and she bared her shins﴾ [27:44] in order to wade through it to Sulayman. Sulayman looked, and she had the most beautiful feet and shins of people, except that she had hair on her shins. When Sulayman saw that, he turned his gaze away from her and called out to her, ﴿He said, "Indeed, it is a palace smoothed, made of glass."﴾ [27:44], that is, smooth, level and even, ﴿made of glass﴾ [27:44], and it is not water. Then Sulayman invited her to Islam. She had seen the state of the throne and the palace, so she responded, and ﴿she said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself"﴾ [27:44], by disbelief. Muqatil said: When she saw the throne and the palace, she knew that Sulayman's kingdom was from Allah, so she said, "My Lord, I have wronged myself by worshipping other than You," ﴿and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [27:44], that is, I have made my monotheism sincere for Him. It was also said: when she reached the palace and thought it was deep water, she said to herself, "Sulayman wants to drown me, and being killed would be easier for me than this." So her saying "I have wronged myself" means by that the suspicion.

They differed about her situation after her conversion. Awn ibn Abd Allah said: A man asked Abd Allah ibn Utbah, "Did Sulayman marry her?" He said, "Her matter ended with her saying, 'I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds,'" meaning: we have no knowledge beyond that. Some of them said: he married her. When he wanted to marry her, he disliked the abundance of hair on her shins that he saw, so he asked mankind, "What removes this?" They said, "The razor." The woman said, "No iron has ever touched me." Sulayman disliked the razor and said, "It would cut her shins." He asked the jinn, and they said, "We do not know." Then he asked the devils, and they said, "We will devise a trick for you until she becomes like white silver," so they made depilatory paste and the bathhouse, and the depilatory paste and bathhouses have existed from that day [[This and similar things are fabrications of the Jews, who depict the prophets as if they had no concern but pleasure and devising means to remove the hair of the shins, to display beauty and satisfy desire. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated a report about this, and Ibn Kathir said of it (3/367): "It is very strange and extremely unusual, and perhaps it is one of the errors of Ata ibn al-Sa'ib on Ibn Abbas, and Allah knows best. The closest explanation in such contexts is that they are taken from the People of the Book, from what is found in their scriptures..."]]. When Sulayman married her, he loved her with an intense love, and he confirmed her in her kingship, and he ordered the jinn, and they built for her in the land of Yemen three fortresses, the like of which people had never seen in height and beauty. They were: Salhin, Baynun and Amdan. Then Sulayman would visit her once a month, after he had returned her to her kingdom, and he would stay with her for three days, travelling early from Syria to Yemen and from Yemen to Syria. It is reported, as mentioned and related from Wahb, who said: They claim that when Bilqis embraced Islam, Sulayman said to her, "Choose a man from your people for me to marry you to." She said, "And should a woman like me, O Prophet of Allah, marry men, when I had in my people such kingship and authority as I had?" He said, "Yes, indeed, in Islam there is nothing but that, and it is not fitting for you to forbid what Allah has made lawful for you." She said, "Marry me, if there must be such a thing, to Dhu Tubba', the king of Hamadhan." So he married her to him, then returned her to Yemen, and he appointed her husband Dhu Tubba' over Yemen, and he summoned Zawba'a, the commander of the jinn of Yemen, and said, "Work for Dhu Tubba' in whatever he assigns you to." He remained a king there, doing with it what he wished, until Sulayman died. When a year had passed and the jinn realized that Sulayman had died, a man from among them came, took the road to Tihama, and when he was in the middle of Yemen, he cried out at the top of his voice, "O company of jinn, indeed King Sulayman has died, so lift your hands." They lifted their hands and dispersed, and the kingdom of Dhu Tubba' ended, and the kingdom of Bilqis ended along with the kingdom of Sulayman [[See what has been quoted above from the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, commenting on these narrations.]]. It was also said: the kingship reached Sulayman when he was thirteen years old, and he died when he was fifty-three years old.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 45–47:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And We certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying]: "Worship Allah"﴾ [i.e., "that" (an, the explanatory particle)] ﴿Worship Allah﴾ alone, ﴿but they became two factions [one believing and one disbelieving] ﴿disputing﴾ concerning the religion. Muqatil said: Their dispute is what is mentioned in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿The eminent ones who were arrogant among his people said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed﴾ up to His saying: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:75–77). So Salih said to them: ﴿O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good?﴾ meaning, to hasten punishment and retribution, ﴿before [the] good?﴾ meaning, well-being and mercy. ﴿Why not seek forgiveness of Allah?﴾ meaning, why do you not (halla) ask forgiveness of Allah through repentance from your disbelief, ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾. ﴿They said: "We see an omen in you and in those with you."﴾ That is, we consider you a bad omen (tashaamanna), and its original form is tataiyyarna. ﴿It was said that they only said this because their word had been divided. And it was said: because he withheld the rain from them at that time and they suffered drought, so they said: "This harm and hardship has befallen us because of your ill omen and the ill omen of your companions."

﴿He said: "Your omen is with Allah"﴾ meaning, what befalls you of good and evil is with Allah by His command, and it is written for you. It was called a bird (ta'ir) because of the swiftness of its descent upon a person, for nothing is swifter than a decreed, inevitable decree. Ibn Abbas said: "The ill omen came to you from Allah because of your disbelief." It was also said: "Your omen" means your deeds with Allah, and it was called a bird because of the swiftness of its ascent to the heaven.

﴿Rather, you are a people being tested﴾. Ibn Abbas said: you are being tested with good and evil. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:35]. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "You are being punished."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 60–61:

﴿Is He not [better] who created the heavens and the earth?﴾ Its meaning: Are your gods better, or He who created the heavens and the earth? ﴿And sent down for you water from the sky﴾ meaning the rain, ﴿and We caused to grow thereby gardens﴾ ? Basātīn (orchards), the plural of ḥadīqah (garden). Al-Farrā' said: the ḥadīqah is an orchard that is enclosed by a wall; if it has no wall, it is not a ḥadīqah. ﴿Full of delight﴾ i.e., of beautiful sight, and al-bahjah (delight) is the beauty by which whoever sees it is delighted. ﴿It was not for you to grow its trees﴾ i.e., it is not fitting for you, because you are not able to do it.

﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ This is an interrogative in the manner of denial: Is there with Him any other deity that helped Him in His making? Rather, there is no god with Him.

﴿Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals (to Him)﴾ meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿who ascribe equals﴾ i.e., who associate partners.

﴿Is He not [better] who made the earth a place of stability﴾ not shaking with its inhabitants, ﴿and placed within it rivers﴾ in its midst [[Omitted from "A".]] ﴿and placed for it firm mountains﴾ fixed mountains, ﴿and placed between the two seas﴾ the sweet and the salt, ﴿a barrier﴾

preventing one of them from mixing with the other. ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Nay, but most of them do not know﴾ the Oneness of their Lord and His authority.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 62–65:

﴿Or who answers the distressed one (al-mudtarr), the afflicted and burdened, when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil (al-su')﴾, that is, the harm (al-darr)[[Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that He is the one called upon in times of hardship and the one hoped in during calamities, as He says: "And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him" [17:67], and He says: "Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out" [16:53]. Likewise He says here: "Or who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him", meaning: who is it that the distressed one turns to only Him, and who removes the harm of the afflicted other than Him? See Tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) Ibn Kathir: (3 / 371–372), where he cites a number of hadiths on this meaning.]] ﴿and makes you successors (khulafa') of the earth﴾, its inhabitants. He destroys one generation and brings forth another. It is also said: He makes your children your successors. And it is said: He made you successors of the jinn on the earth.

﴿Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember﴾. Abu 'Amr read it with the ya' (يَتَذَكَّرُونَ, "they remember"), and the others read it with the ta' (تَذَكَّرُونَ, "you remember").[[That is: Is there a god with Allah who is able to do that? Or is there a god with Allah after this, when it is known that Allah alone is the one who does this, with no partner? "Little do you remember", meaning: how little they remember what would guide them to the truth and lead them to the straight path. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3 / 372.]]

﴿Or who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾ when you travel, ﴿and who sends the winds as good news before His mercy﴾, that is, before the rain, ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾

﴿Or who originates creation and then repeats it﴾ after death, ﴿and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth﴾, that is, from the heaven the rain and from the earth the plants.

﴿Is there a god with Allah? Say: Bring your proof﴾, your evidence for your claim that there is another god with Allah, ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾. It was revealed concerning the polytheists, when they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the time of the Hour.[[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3 / 373–374; and Alam al-Ghayb wa al-Shahadah fi al-Tasawwur al-Islami (The Knower of the Unseen and the Witnessed in the Islamic Conception) by Uthman Jum'ah Dumairiyyah, pp. (78–81) and (86–91).]] ﴿and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 69–76:

﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the criminals."﴾ ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ over their denial of you and their turning away from you. ﴿And do not be in distress over what they plan﴾. It was revealed concerning the mockers who divided up the punishments of Makkah.

﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"﴾ ﴿Say, "Perhaps it has drawn near to you"﴾ i.e., it has approached and come close. ﴿Some of what you seek to hasten﴾. It was said: it has followed you, and the meaning is "it has followed you" (radifa lakum); the lam was added as it was added in His saying, "for their Lord they fear" [al-A'raf: 154]. Al-Farra' said: the lam is an extra, connective particle, as you say, "I paid him a hundred" and "I paid for him." ﴿Some of what you seek to hasten﴾ of the punishment, and that befell them on the day of Badr.

﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward the people﴾. Muqatil said: toward the people of Makkah, in that He did not hasten the punishment upon them. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾ for that.

﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal﴾ what they hide ﴿and what they reveal﴾. ﴿And there is not an unseen thing﴾ i.e., any hidden thing of concealed secret, any concealed matter, or any unseen thing ﴿in the heaven or the earth except that it is in a clear register﴾ i.e., in the Preserved Tablet.

﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel﴾ i.e., clarifies for them ﴿most of that over which they differ﴾ concerning matters of religion. Al-Kalbi said: the People of the Book differed among themselves, becoming factions that attacked one another, so the Qur'an was revealed to clarify what they differed about.

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil (The Landmarks of Revelation) of al-Baghawi on Surah 27, verses 77–81:**

﴿And indeed it﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿is surely a guidance and a mercy for the believers.﴾ ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge﴾ means He will decide ﴿between them﴾, that is, between those who differ in religion, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿by His judgment﴾, which is the truth, ﴿and He is the Mighty﴾, the Invincible, so none of His decrees is ever reversed, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their conditions, so nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿So put your trust in Allah. Indeed you are upon the manifest truth﴾, the clear truth.

﴿Indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ means the disbelievers, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾. Ibn Kathir recited ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُ﴾ (*la yasma'u*, "does not hear") with a *ya* and with a *fatha* on it, and with a *fatha* on the *mim* of ﴿الصُّمُّ﴾ (*al-summu*, "the deaf"), making it in the nominative. He recited the same in Surat al-Rum. The rest recited ﴿لَا تُسْمِعُ﴾ (*la tusmi'u*, "you do not make hear") with a *ta* and a *damma* on it, and a *kasra* on the *mim*, making ﴿الصُّمَّ﴾ (*as-summa*, "the deaf") in the accusative.

﴿When they turn their backs, retreating﴾, that is, turning away. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿when they turn their backs, retreating﴾, since if they are deaf and do not hear, it makes no difference whether they turn away or not? It was said: it is mentioned for emphasis and intensification. It was also said: a deaf person who is present may hear when the voice is raised and understand by signs, but when he turns away he neither hears nor understands. Qatadah said: "When a deaf person turns his back and you call him, he does not hear. Likewise the disbeliever does not hear what he is called to of faith." The meaning of the verse is that, because of their extreme aversion to what they are called to, they are like the dead, whom there is no way to make hear, and like the deaf, who do not hear.

﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their error.﴾ Al-A'mash and Hamzah recited ﴿تَهْدِي﴾ (*tahdi*, "you guide") with a *ta* and a *fatha*, as a verb, with ﴿الْعُمْيَ﴾ (*al-'umya*, "the blind") in the accusative on the *ya* here and in al-Rum. The others recited ﴿بِهَادِي﴾ (*bihadi*, "guider") with a *ba* as a noun, and ﴿الْعُمْيِ﴾ (*al-'umyi*, "the blind") with a *kasra* on the *ya*. ﴿Away from their error﴾ means: you are not one who guides someone whom Allah has blinded to guidance, and whose heart He has blinded to faith. ﴿You can make hear only﴾ what you make hear, ﴿those who believe in Our signs﴾, only those who affirm that the Qur'an is from Allah, ﴿and they are submitters﴾, sincere ones.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 83–84:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We gather from every nation a troop﴾ meaning, from every generation (qarn) a company, ﴿of those who denied Our signs﴾. Here "min" (from) is not partitive (lil-tab'id), because all those who denied will be gathered, ﴿and they will be driven on﴾, meaning, their first will be held back until their last, until they are assembled, and then they will be driven to the Fire.

﴿Until, when they arrive﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿He will say﴾, meaning Allah will say to them: ﴿Did you deny My signs while not encompassing them in knowledge﴾, meaning, while you did not know them with true knowledge, ﴿or what was it that you were doing?﴾, meaning, when you did not reflect upon them. The meaning of the verse is: Did you deny My signs without knowing them, and without reflecting on their truth, but rather you denied them in ignorance?

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verse 85–87:

﴿And the word will come into effect﴾ meaning the punishment will be due, ﴿against them because they wronged﴾ meaning because they associated partners (with Allah), ﴿so they will not speak﴾. Qatadah said: How can they speak when they have no argument? A parallel to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to offer excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. It was also said: they will not speak because their mouths will be sealed.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Have they not seen that We made﴾ meaning created ﴿the night for them to rest therein, and the day to give sight?﴾ meaning illuminating, in which one can see. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ meaning who affirm, so they take heed.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Day the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾. The Ṣūr is a horn into which Israfil will blow. Al-Hasan said: the Ṣūr is the horn. Some of them interpreted his words to mean that the spirits are gathered into the horn, then it is blown into, so the spirits go to the bodies and the bodies come to life. His saying: ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾ means: they will be struck dead (faṣaʿiqa), as He said in another verse: "And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon" [al-Zumar: 68], meaning they will die. The meaning is that terror will be cast upon them until they die. It was also said: Israfil will blow into the Ṣūr three blasts: the blast of terror, the blast of swooning, and the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. [Al-Tabari narrated a lengthy hadith on this, traced to the Prophet: 20/19.]

He says: Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, Jibril, Mika'il and the Angel of Death remain. He says: Take the soul of Mika'il, and he takes his soul, and he falls like a mighty mountain. He says: Who remains? He says: Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, Jibril and the Angel of Death remain. He says: Die, O Angel of Death, and he dies. He says: O Jibril, who remains? He says: Blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, Your Face remains, lasting and eternal, and Jibril is the dying, perishing one. He said: He says, O Jibril, there must be your death too, and he falls prostrate, beating his wings. It is narrated that the excellence of His creation over the excellence of Mika'il is like a mighty mountain over a small hill [[Narrated by al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in "al-Ibanah", and Ibn Mardawayh from Anas. (2373): 4/1843-1844, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 15/105. His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And all will come to Him﴾ meaning those who were brought back to life after death. ﴿Coming﴾: al-A'mash, Hamzah and Hafs recited "atawhu" with a shortened alif and a fathah on the ta', as a verb, meaning they came to Him. The others recited it with a long vowel and a damma on the ta', like His saying: ﴿And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 95]. ﴿Humbled﴾ meaning abased.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 88–89:**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾. *Qā'imatan* (standing) and *wāqifatan* (stationary). ﴿While they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾, meaning: they move as clouds move until they fall upon the earth, and then they become level with it. That is because every great thing and every large gathering whose extent the eye cannot take in, owing to its vastness and the distance between its extremities, appears to the observer as stationary while it is in motion. Likewise, the movement of the mountains will not be seen on the Day of Resurrection because of their magnitude, just as the movement of the clouds is not seen because of their greatness while they are moving. ﴿The handiwork of Allah﴾: *ṣun'a* is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*maṣdar*). ﴿Who has perfected everything﴾, meaning: who has made it firm and sound. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra recited it with *yā'* (they), and the rest with *tā'* (you).

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾ — with the word of sincere monotheism (*kalimat al-ikhlāṣ*), which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Abu Ma'shar said: Ibrahim used to swear without making an exception, saying: "The good deed is 'There is no god but Allah.'" Qatadah said: "[It is] sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*)." It has also been said: [it is] every act of obedience. [See: al-Tabari: 20/22–23. There is no contradiction between these statements, for the word of tawhid, "the testimony that there is no god but Allah," is the word of sincerity, and there is no obedience without sincerity. And Allah knows best.] ﴿Then he will have something better than it﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "From it, good reaches him," meaning: from that good deed he receives the good of the Day of Resurrection, which is the reward and safety from punishment. As for whether he may have something better than faith, the answer is no, because there is nothing better than his saying "There is no god but Allah." It has also been said: "Then he will have something better than it," meaning: the good pleasure of Allah, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And the good pleasure of Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72]. Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "Then he will have something better than it," meaning: multiples; Allah, Exalted, gives him ten or more for one. (Refer to the earlier discussion in the tafsir of surah al-An'am: 3/210–211.) This is good, because multiplication has distinctive features: among them, the servant is questioned about his deed but is not questioned about the multiples; among them, Satan has a path to his deed but has no path to the multiples; there is no hope for adversaries regarding the multiples; and because the good deed is according to the servant's merit, while the multiplication is in keeping with the generosity of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted.

﴿And they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾. The people of Kufa read *min faza'in* with tanwin and *yawma'idhin* with a fatha on the *mīm*; the others read it with the *iḍāfa* (construct), because it is more general, for it implies safety from all the terror of that Day, whereas with tanwin it is as if it were one terror and not another. The people of Medina pronounce the *mīm* of *yawma'idhin* with a fatha.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 27, verses 90–93:

﴿Whoever comes with the evil deed﴾, meaning shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾, meaning they will be thrown onto their faces. It is said: "I overturned (kabbabtu) the man," when I threw him onto his face, so he fell on his face (infakaba) and was overturned (akabba). The keepers of Hell will say to them: ﴿Are you being repaid except for what you used to do?﴾, that is, the shirk you committed in the world.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I have only been commanded﴾. God says to His Messenger (ﷺ): Say, "I have only been commanded ﴿to worship the Lord of this city﴾", meaning Makkah, ﴿who has made it sacred﴾, that is, God made it a sanctuary (haram) and a safe place, where no blood is shed, no one is wronged, its game is not hunted, and ۝ its grass is not cut (yukhtala khalaha). ﴿To Him belongs everything﴾ in creation and in ownership. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, meaning submitting to God.

﴿And to recite the Qur'an﴾, meaning: and I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an. ﴿So whoever is guided, he is only guided for his own self﴾, that is, the benefit of his guidance returns to him. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ from faith and strays from the path of guidance, ﴿then say: I am only one of the warners﴾, one of those who give fear. There is no duty upon me except conveying (the message). It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. [[See above: 1/32–33, note (1).]]

﴿And say: Praise belongs to God﴾ for His blessings. ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning on the Day of Badr, of killing, captivity, and striking [60/b]
